jobs.prompt: Add swarm update --when-idle [--timeout MINUTES] (default 60). Today swarm update is refused while any run, go loop or busy marker is live, and a long wave loop (go --scope) is only idle for a few seconds between waves, so the owner cannot catch a gap by hand; the Mac mini update was refused for that reason while an atlas-seafloor run was going. With --when-idle the update waits for the gap at a wave boundary instead of refusing, and holds new work back so the gap is real. Mechanism: swarm update --when-idle writes an update-pending record in the install root (a small file, mode 0600, atomic: pid of the waiting update, startedAt, expiresAt = start + timeout, the target tag if known) and removes it on every exit path (success, failure, Ctrl-C, timeout) and ignores it when its pid is dead or it is expired (stale records never block anything). While the record is valid: (a) every launcher of NEW work checks it before starting and waits (poll every 2 seconds, printing waiting for swarm update, at most until the record expires or disappears) instead of starting: the wave loop (go --scope: the step that prepares and starts the next wave, in the deps wiring of the go scope loop), swarm autopilot start-ready, swarm run, swarm go and any command that launches workers; commands that only read or that finish live runs (integrate, sync, cancel, status, watch, resume of an already running run) are not held; (b) live runs are never killed or paused: the update waits until no run is live and no busy marker is alive (the same idle test the plain update uses, with the busy markers written by the held launchers excluded), checking every 2 seconds and printing one status line every 30 seconds saying what it waits for (the run ids and commands); (c) at the first idle moment it performs the normal update exactly as today (including the pointer bump, the server restart from the previous change, and the pin rules), then removes the record so held launchers continue, and they continue on the new version because they start their next step through the installed current runner (if a held launcher is an in-memory loop of the OLD version it simply continues with old code; that is fine and must not crash); (d) on timeout it removes the record, prints that the update did not run because the machine never became idle within N minutes, names what was still live, and exits with code 75 (try again); a normal update without --when-idle behaves exactly as before (refused while busy). --when-idle with --projects is refused with a clear message. A second concurrent --when-idle update is refused (one pending record at a time) with the pid of the first. Add the flag to the help text and the command metadata used by completions so tests/completion.test.mjs passes. Tests in tests/update-when-idle.test.mjs, hermetic (temp install root and HOME, fake runs and busy markers made with the existing marker helpers, tiny poll intervals injected, no real runs, no network, no ambient environment): update --when-idle with a live marker waits and then updates when the marker is removed (and the held launcher simulation waits while the record exists and continues after); the record is removed on success, on failure, on timeout and on abort; a stale record (dead pid or expired) never blocks a launcher or an update; timeout exits 75 and names what was live; a read-only command is not held; the plain update is still refused while busy; two concurrent --when-idle updates: the second is refused; the held launcher is released at the timeout even if the update process died; status lines appear on a long wait. Keep every existing test passing. Respect the import cycle rule: new modules must not statically import install.mjs. No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: tests that reference swarm.mjs in passing are covered by the full suite run before merge.
